metadata.direction_rule: Tractability is scored in the direction the signature wants, not in the direction the target class is usually drugged. Where a receptor or channel must be potentiated (GABA-A subunits, Kv7, SV2A) the precedent is high. Where an enzyme, transporter or channel must be RAISED (GAD1/2, KCC2, EAAT2, Kir4.1, Nav1.1) the precedent is inhibitors or nothing, so it is scored as the harder activation problem.
metadata.purpose: Per-target modality annotation for epilepsy. Tells the design layer which proteins a small molecule can realistically engage.

schema.small_molecule_tractability: 0-1 ordinal prior that a drug-like small molecule can productively engage this protein; 0 marks a transcriptional readout rather than a target
schema.note: the reason for the value, so it can be argued with

metadata.curation_rule: Ordinal priors reflecting precedent in the public literature, on the same scale as the MS, Parkinson's and Alzheimer's annotations. Judgements, not measurements.
metadata.readout_convention: A target scoring below 0.2 is treated by the design engine as a readout: the profile may require its expression to move, but no arm of a designed molecule will be assigned to bind it.
metadata.the_defining_problem: Epilepsy is the opposite case to Alzheimer's. The disease-defining targets are ion channels and receptors, which are the most tractable protein class there is: most of the approved drugs already act on them. The unmet need is therefore not in tractability but in what those targets do not reach. About a third of patients are drug-resistant, no approved drug prevents epileptogenesis, and the axes with the least chemical matter (astroglial buffering, adenosine, mTOR pathway correction) sit on targets that are enzymes, suppressors or structural proteins. The profile tests whether the engine can look past the crowded channel targets.

ABAT.note: GABA transaminase; vigabatrin is an irreversible inhibitor

ADK.note: Adenosine kinase; inhibitors are well-characterised, and inhibition is the wanted direction

ADORA1.note: A1 receptor; agonists have precedent but a heavy sedative and cardiac cost

ADORA2A.note: A2A receptor antagonists, with istradefylline as approved precedent

AKT1.note: Inhibition is the wanted direction here, and inhibitors are clinical-stage

AQP4.note: Water channel with mislocalisation in hippocampal sclerosis; modulators are early-stage

BCL2.note: Raising the anti-apoptotic protein is wanted, and the small-molecule precedent is inhibition

BDNF.note: Pro-epileptogenic here, so lowering it is wanted, and it is reached through TrkB rather than bound

CA2.note: Carbonic anhydrase II; acetazolamide, topiramate and zonisamide

CACNA1A.note: P/Q-type Cav2.1; partly inhibited by lamotrigine and levetiracetam

CACNA2D1.note: Alpha-2-delta-1; gabapentin and pregabalin bind it

CHRNA4.note: Nicotinic alpha-4; the target of a gain-of-function familial epilepsy

DEPDC5.note: GATOR1 component, a loss-of-function epilepsy gene; restoration is not a small-molecule goal

FOS.note: An immediate-early-gene readout of neuronal activity

GABRA1.note: GABA-A alpha-1; benzodiazepine and barbiturate potentiation is the best-precedented mechanism in the disease

GABRA5.note: GABA-A alpha-5, extrasynaptic tonic inhibition; subtype-selective positive modulators exist

GABRB3.note: GABA-A beta-3; barbiturate and loreclezole-type sites

GABRD.note: GABA-A delta, extrasynaptic; neurosteroids (ganaxolone) potentiate it

GABRG2.note: GABA-A gamma-2, required for the benzodiazepine site

GAD1.note: GABA synthesis; enzyme induction rather than activation is wanted, and there is no small-molecule precedent

GJA1.note: Connexin 43; gap-junction blockers such as tonabersat exist

GLUL.note: Glutamine synthetase; loss in hippocampal sclerosis, activation is not a realistic small-molecule goal

GPR55.note: Cannabidiol antagonises it; few selective ligands

GRIA1.note: AMPA subunit; perampanel is the approved noncompetitive antagonist

GRIK2.note: Kainate subunit; topiramate acts at it, selective agents are scarce

GRIN1.note: Obligatory NMDA subunit; ketamine and memantine-type blockers

GRIN2A.note: NMDA subunit; selective negative modulators exist

GRM5.note: mGluR5, with negative allosteric modulators in clinical development

HDAC1.note: Histone deacetylase; valproate is a weak inhibitor

HMGB1.note: Alarmin; antibodies and glycyrrhizin-type binders only

IL1B.note: A cytokine, reached through the inflammasome or receptor antagonism

IL1R1.note: Anakinra blocks it; small-molecule antagonists are rare

IL6.note: A cytokine, a readout of glial activation

KCNA1.note: Kv1.1; opening is wanted, and openers are rare

KCNJ10.note: Kir4.1, whose astroglial loss is the wanted direction to reverse; openers are rare

KCNMA1.note: BK channel; openers exist but a mixed effect on excitability

KCNQ2.note: Kv7.2; retigabine and azetukalner open it, and opening is the wanted direction

KCNT1.note: Gain-of-function epilepsy target; inhibitors such as quinidine are nonselective

NEFL.note: Neurofilament light, an injury biomarker and a readout

NPY.note: A peptide, delivered or induced rather than bound; raising it is the wanted direction

P2RX7.note: ATP-gated channel upstream of the inflammasome, with brain-penetrant antagonists in clinical development

PPARA.note: Fibrate target; agonism is the wanted direction

PTEN.note: Restoring a lost phosphatase is not a small-molecule goal

SCN1A.note: Nav1.1; activation is wanted (Dravet), and activators are peptide toxins and early tool compounds. Sodium blockers can worsen Dravet

SCN1B.note: Sodium-channel beta-1 subunit, a structural readout

SCN2A.note: Nav1.2; blocked by the classic sodium-channel antiseizure drugs

SCN3A.note: Nav1.3; blocked by the same class

SCN8A.note: Nav1.6; the target of the newer isoform-selective inhibitors

SLC12A2.note: NKCC1; bumetanide inhibits it, and inhibition is the wanted direction

SLC12A5.note: KCC2; raising chloride extrusion is wanted and enhancers are disputed tool compounds

SLC1A2.note: EAAT2; raising uptake is wanted and activators are early-stage

SLC1A3.note: EAAT1; as EAAT2, activation is the wanted direction

SLC2A1.note: GLUT1; raising glucose transport is wanted and the ketogenic route bypasses it

SLC6A1.note: GAT-1; tiagabine is the approved inhibitor, and inhibition is the wanted direction

SOD2.note: Mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme, induced rather than bound

STXBP1.note: Munc18-1; haploinsufficiency, and no route to raising it by small molecule

SV2A.note: The levetiracetam and brivaracetam binding site, with a well-characterised ligand series

TRPV1.note: Antagonists and desensitising agonists are well-precedented

TSC1.note: Tumour suppressor whose loss drives mTOR; restoring it is not a small-molecule goal
